items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Hitler was in power then, so anyway we were standing in the station and all them German soldiers, everywhere you saw was uniforms.

ctx.x: Was this the first time -- was this 1933 or '39?

'39. It was '39, 1939. Hitler was in power then, so anyway we were standing in the station and all them German soldiers, everywhere you saw was uniforms. Youknow, they took our pullmans, the man had paid for them -- we stayed in that station from 11 o'clock in the morning until 12 o'clock at night, because they took all the transportation for the soldiers. They were moving then. That's right.

So one day we were standing up in the station and them guys in the German Air Corps, they call them Luftwaffe, they were the sharpest cats you ever saw. Them cats were so sharp, them uniforms, they was sharp, daddy. Young cats. I was standing there with Johnny Hodges and Toby and I had a little bottle
